original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.
Only changing helper terminal subspaces and monotone frames within the fixed scalar word, entrances and cleanup contract already covered by #1995/#2013.

Searching below C=40 in the #2017 Eisenstein binary scalar-rectangle or fixed-support block-linear additive pairing model; specify a changed premise instead. This bound does not cover every complex decoder.

actual_scope: On the pinned gauge44 local program (selected-replay.tar.gz member candidate/strict/global/base/providers/gauge44/LOCAL-PROGRAMS.json.gz), screen the complete family of disjoint fusions of consecutive same-column rank-(1,1) climb pairs into rank-2 children, with the intervening referencing events retimed for free, parameterized by the number of intervening referencing events (touch depth 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and unrestricted). Report the maximum disjoint matching per depth by two algorithms and the exact ceiling of the resulting optimistic profile against the recomputed 5% gate.
scope_change_reason: The generic rank-shape card is saturated; this is the exact first step named by research/complex-rank2-retiming-seed73506's open question 1 (pairs with two intervening scalar operations), extended in one parameter (touch depth) on the same pinned word and the same profile shape {1: 2412-2n, 2: 418+n, 3: 432, 4: 142, 5: 82, 8: 8}. The predecessor restricted to one intervening scalar event and stopped at 674 of the 720 fusions its screen requires.
existing_restriction_changed: The predecessor's one-touch restriction (exactly one intervening referencing scalar event). All retiming, copy, frame, hosting, precision, interface and restoration costs stay waived, exactly as in the predecessor's favorable screen.
bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of the binding complex side's recursive cost. Fusing same-column rank-1 climb pairs into rank-2 children moves paid mass to larger children and raises the packing ceiling of the unchanged selected word; the capacity of that family, at each retiming depth, decides whether the lever is reachable before any physical bill.
method: Independent stdlib-only reconstruction of both orientations' climb paths and referencing events from the pinned literal event archive; touch-depth classification of all consecutive climb pairs; maximum vertex-disjoint matchings per class by leftmost greedy and an independent path DP; exact rational ceiling brackets via the pinned research/complex-local-word-ceiling/ceiling.py at m = 73, 896 families, 9 stages, centre 64; recomputed 5% target and least passing fusion count; published anchors and failure controls in verify.py.
optimistic_budget: Zero-extra-charge relaxation of the predecessor: every fusion is granted free, all incumbent charges stay. The full family's optimistic ceiling (+6.37%) is this family's upper bound; a physical bill must come out of that margin.
required_improvement: Certified ceiling at least 5% above the selected word's certified upper endpoint (target a = 0.00177455681454345); the profile shape needs at least 720 disjoint fusions for that.
stop_rule: Stop when even the favorable zero-overhead profile of a class is certified below the 5% target, and record the exact obstruction (max matching versus the fusion threshold).
outcome_summary: Completed scoped negative/positive capacity line. Anchors reproduced exactly (2,782 adjacent pairs, 1,441 (1,1) pairs, touch distribution {1:690, 2:473, 3:136, 4:66, 5:72, ge6:4}, one-touch 690 candidates / 674 matched, threshold 720 with 719 certified fail). Extension: touch <= 2 gives 1,163 candidates and 716 disjoint fusions, still certified below the 5% gate (gain 4.9712%); touch <= 3 is the first depth whose capacity passes (1,299 candidates, 790 matched, gain 5.5134%); the unrestricted family caps at 905 disjoint fusions (gain 6.3673%). Both orientations agree.
evidence: research/complex-rank2-touch-depth-seed06773f60/RESULT.json (exact rationals), verify.py markers PASS_RANK2_TOUCH_DEPTH and PASS_CONTROLS; exact rational ceiling brackets from the pinned ceiling engine; threshold controls 719/720; touch-bin-mutation and inflated-target failure controls; greedy/DP cross-check with vertex-disjointness.
falsification_test: The two-touch hypothesis of the predecessor's open question was falsified at the capacity level before any map check: even with every retiming and implementation charge waived, 716 < 720 disjoint fusions is certified below the 5% gate (early kill per autoresearch section 4). The smallest-instance value-map check is therefore recorded as not attempted for two-touch; for three-touch (capacity-surviving) it is the open obligation.

open_questions.question: Does a legal retiming transformation exist for three-touch (1,1) pairs, carrying both dirty dependencies through three referencing events without a paid rank-1 child?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Touch depth 3 is the first class whose capacity (790 >= 720) can pass the ideal 5% gate; without a legality lemma the surviving capacity is unusable.
open_questions.first_step: Pick one concrete three-touch (1,1) window from RESULT.json's class-3 candidate set and write its exact frame/value bookkeeping for a rank-2 child with free scalar work.
open_questions.blocked_by: The pinned event schema records frame transitions and scalar references but no documented dirty-state map contract for fusing across referencing events.

open_questions.question: Do mixed-rank adjacent climb pairs (1,341 non-(1,1) pairs of the 2,782) raise the family ceiling past the gate with fewer fusions?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Fusing a (1,2) pair yields a rank-3 child; the rank-dependent per-fusion gain could beat the rank-2-only shape that needs 720 fusions.
open_questions.first_step: Weighted matching on all 2,782 adjacent pairs with each fusion priced by its exact ceiling delta, then re-screen.
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing blocks the screen; it is a bounded follow-up computation, not attempted here.

open_questions.question: How much added paid rank can the surviving classes absorb before missing the 5% gate?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The unrestricted family's ideal margin is only 6.37% versus the 5% gate, so the physical bill has little room; an allowed-overhead budget converts the screen into a design target.
open_questions.first_step: Charge a uniform added rank delta per fusion and solve for the largest delta that keeps the certified ceiling above the target at n = 790 and n = 905.
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing blocks it; not attempted in this session.
